title: MOS small-signal model and analysis procedure

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
Transistor circuits are non-linear, but for small signals around a fixed bias point they behave linearly. The **small-signal model** replaces the device with linear elements whose values come from the operating point: a voltage-controlled current source \(g_mv_{gs}\) from drain to source, the output resistance \(r_o\) in parallel, and an open circuit at the insulated gate (capacitors are added at high frequency).

The **procedure** is always the same. First solve the DC bias and confirm the region. Second, compute \(g_m\) and \(r_o\) at that point. Third, redraw the circuit with every transistor replaced by its model, DC voltage sources shorted and DC current sources opened, since constants have no incremental part. Fourth, solve the linear circuit for gains and impedances. The model is valid while the signal is small compared with the overdrive, \(|v_{gs}| \ll 2V_{ov}\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ i_d = g_mv_{gs} + \frac{v_{ds}}{r_o} \]
\[ \text{DC } V \to \text{short}, \quad \text{DC } I \to \text{open}, \quad \frac{\Delta I_{\text{exact}} - g_mv_{gs}}{g_mv_{gs}} = \frac{v_{gs}}{2V_{ov}} \]
sections.figure_alt: Square-law I_D versus V_GS with the tangent line drawn at the bias point; the tangent's slope is the transconductance g_m.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A device has \(g_m = 3\ \mathrm{mS}\) and \(r_o = 40\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). A disturbance gives \(v_{gs} = -2\ \mathrm{mV}\) and \(v_{ds} = +0.2\ \mathrm{V}\): \(i_d = -6\ \mu\mathrm{A} + 5\ \mu\mathrm{A} = -1\ \mu\mathrm{A}\). With \(V_{ov} = 0.3\ \mathrm{V}\), the 2 mV step is far below \(2V_{ov}\), so the linear model is accurate to about 0.3%.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Building the model before solving the bias point.
- Leaving DC sources in the small-signal circuit, or opening a voltage source instead of shorting it.
- Getting signs wrong when the source node moves: \(v_{gs} = v_g - v_s\).

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: The same model, with sign care, covers PMOS devices. Adding capacitors and the body transconductance extends it to high frequency and four terminals, and applying it to whole circuits gives the CS, CG and CD amplifiers.
